review_candidates.title: Software Engineer
review_candidates.description: About The Company The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) serves as the university computing center for the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and functions as a leading IT and computing competence center for the Max Planck Society. With over 40 years of experience, GWDG specializes in providing high-performance computing systems and IT infrastructure to support cutting-edge research across various scientific disciplines. In 2020, GWDG was recognized as one of eight national high-performance computing centers within the German NHR network, emphasizing its prominence in the field. The organization also operates the national AI service center KISSKI and collaborates on the EU AI Factory HammerHAI initiative. Additionally, GWDG supports the German Aerospace Center (DLR) by providing HPC resources and plays a vital role in advancing digital science and technology. Its services cater to researchers and students in digital humanities, life sciences, earth system sciences, and engineering, fostering innovation through national and international research projects. The GWDG is actively involved in quantum computing initiatives, notably through the QUICS project, which offers SMEs access to quantum computing resources, positioning itself at the forefront of technological development. About The Role We are seeking a highly skilled Quantum Software Engineer (m/f/d) to join our interdisciplinary HPC team within the "Computing" working group at GWDG. This full-time position (39 hours per week) is funded through the GWDG QC project, which is scheduled to run until October 2029. The primary focus of this role is to contribute to the development of GWDG’s quantum computing ecosystem, particularly in the area of anomaly detection for industrial applications. The successful candidate will play a crucial role in building a platform that leverages quantum computing for industry-specific use cases, providing companies with advanced tools for quantum anomaly detection. The role requires a deep understanding of software architecture, containerization, and high-performance computing environments, combined with a strong commitment to security and data privacy standards. The candidate will work closely with research scientists, developers, and industry partners to design, implement, and optimize scalable, secure, and efficient quantum computing solutions. Qualifications The ideal candidate will possess a PhD and/or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Physics, or a related field, complemented by demonstrable research or industry experience. Proven coding skills are essential, particularly in developing complex software without AI assistance, including knowledge of scope, functions, variables, classes, and array methods. Experience in designing and managing software architecture for containerized systems, such as Docker or Kubernetes, is required. Familiarity with heterogeneous APIs and integration of HPC scheduler systems like SLURM is also necessary. Knowledge of quantum computing job characteristics, resource requirements, and familiarity with compiler or transpiler pipelines will be highly advantageous. Candidates should have a solid understanding of encryption, data protection standards, and GDPR compliance. Excellent teamwork and communication skills, along with fluency in English (spoken and written), are essential for success in this role. Responsibilities The core responsibilities of this role include implementing a containerized FullStaQD platform as a reference solution within the project landscape. This involves designing a modular and scalable infrastructure that can support diverse use cases and data workflows. The candidate will establish Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines and automated testing frameworks to ensure software quality and reliability. Handling heterogeneous APIs and integrating HPC scheduler systems such as SLURM will be critical to the platform’s functionality. Ensuring compliance with data privacy and security standards, including DSGVO (GDPR), by implementing encryption and secure data handling practices, is a key aspect of the role. The candidate will also collaborate with team members to optimize performance, troubleshoot issues, and contribute to ongoing research and development efforts related to quantum computing and anomaly detection. Additionally, participation in knowledge sharing and documentation to facilitate platform adoption and future enhancements is expected. Benefits GWDG offers a flexible working environment with options for partial remote work, supporting work-life balance. Employees benefit from working in a modern, diverse, and stimulating environment that bridges academia and industry. The position provides opportunities for professional growth and skill development through participation in innovative projects and collaborations. As a public sector employer, GWDG offers comprehensive social benefits, including pension schemes, health insurance, and continued education support. The organization promotes a culture of diversity and inclusion, encouraging applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities. Working at GWDG means being part of a leading national and international research community dedicated to advancing digital science and technology. Equal Opportunity GWDG is committed to promoting gender equity and diversity within its workforce. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and strongly encourage individuals with disabilities to apply. The organization actively strives to create an inclusive environment where all employees can thrive and contribute to innovative research and development. Equal opportunity employment is a fundamental principle at GWDG, and we are dedicated to ensuring fair and nondiscriminatory hiring practices.
